If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to compensate for bearish bias.

If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 5 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% in mid-horizon (8–15 days) to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast in late horizon (16–30 days) to capture momentum carry.

If sentiment is mixed and price is trending downward, subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast in late horizon (16–30 days) to avoid overcorrection.

If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and price is volatile, apply 1–2% smoothing correction across all horizons to dampen noise.
